newsitem.title: USA: White House cut spying on Cuba - report.
newsitem.headline: White House cut spying on Cuba - report.

text.p: The Clinton administration barred U.S. covert operations in Cuba beginning in December 1994 because of the CIA's bad record on the island and to try to smooth ties with Havana, a newspaper reported Tuesday.
"The action restricted U.S. intelligence agents from such activities as actively recruiting new agents and promoting ways to destabilise the government," the Miami Herald said.
The action, among other things, forced the CIA to close a clandestine radio station that was broadcasting into Cuba, the newspaper said, citing unnamed former and current U.S. officials.
The Herald said a White House spokesman declined to respond to questions about the action.

In a separate article on Tuesday, the newspaper, citing U.S. officials familiar with the discussions, reported that Clinton administration officials considered launching a cruise missile attack on a Cuban air base after Cuban MiGs in February shot down two civilian planes from the United States.
Four people died when the Cuban jets downed the light planes operated by the Miami-based Cuban exile group, Brothers to the Rescue.
